name: Dense Vector Cosine Similarity Nearest Neighbors (Top-K ANN)
description: When a user asks a question in an AI assistant, the query is embedded into a dense vector (e.g. 4-dimensional here for illustration, or 384/1536 in prod). We retrieve the top most semantically relevant documentation chunks.
prompt:
When a user asks a question in an AI assistant, the query is embedded into a dense vector (e.g. 4-dimensional here for illustration, or 384/1536 in prod). We retrieve the top most semantically relevant documentation chunks.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: doc_id, title, similarity_score.
Results should be ordered as specified.
golden_sql:
-- Find the top 2 documents closest to the query embedding [0.9, 0.1, 0.25, 0.0]
            WITH scored_docs AS (
                SELECT 
                    doc_id,
                    title,
                    embedding,
                    -- Native SIMD cosine similarity
                    array_cosine_similarity(embedding, [0.9, 0.1, 0.25, 0.0]::FLOAT[4]) AS cosine_score
                FROM doc_embeddings
            )
            SELECT 
                doc_id,
                title,
                ROUND(cosine_score, 4) AS similarity_score
            FROM scored_docs
            ORDER BY cosine_score DESC
            LIMIT 2;
why_it_fails: Models frequently try to calculate cosine similarity manually using dot product divided by norms in SQL, which is slow, verbose, and numerically unstable with zero vectors.
